units.translation: And if anyone wishes to call it a covering, as common usage does, the covering hide, this leather tunic, let him take refuge in Aeschylus, who said
They dwell in woven roofs high in the air.
of the roof (thus Schneidewinus for στέγαις [roofs]) of the Atreidae.
Alas, halls of kings, beloved roofs.
For this roof is never left by the chorus.
The house is frenzied, the roof raves.
I will set fire to the roof.
someone sitting in the roof by the hearth
to this roof of the Atreidae it leans

about Eteocles, who had fallen in battle. Where M has στυγῶν [hating], but with a gloss added by a second hand, εἴργων δηλονότι [obviously warding off], from which Wakefield restored στέγων [protecting] in Silva critica 1. p. 98.
where the scholiast similarly explains it as τὴν θάλατταν εἴργων [warding off the sea]
Pray that the tower protects against the enemy spear.
For protecting the enemies, he chose death in the city
The oar-blade and the course of the linen-sewn ship, protecting the sea from the spear
τὴν θάλατταν εἴργων [warding off the sea]
to go, to walk, to proceed

to go, to walk, to proceed. It is said equally of those approaching and of those departing, and is used either absolutely or constructed with an accusative of place, or with the prepositions διά, ἐπί, πρός.
The hoplite man goes up the steps of the ladder toward the tower of the enemies.
Such a rush from Zeus, producing fear, comes upon me.
For some go toward the towers.
The down goes just now through the cheeks.
Go, you and the elders, to the houses.
What gathering of women is this that goes?
Having poured out these things, I go
going self-laden with his own baggage to Argos
But I must go first to show the chambers to the holy light of these escorts.
Safety is for those who go through the city.
to one sleeping, walking, and sitting
Passive, of one who is dismissed and departs.
στέλλειν [to send] with the accusative κέλευθον [way] added.
Of sending or moving an army.
as ὁδὸν στέλλεσθαι [to prepare one's way] is said: see Thesaurus vol. 7 p. 698.
στέλλεται [is sent] is corrupt for τέλλεται [is accomplished].
Clearly your word sends me back home.
to send as quickly as possible; for these oracles father Zeus instills in Loxias.
I sent this way from the house
Having furled the sail, she will row with all strength.
How then does he bid him come equipped?
